title: Hearing Armstrong and the New Orleans players; dropping the saxophone
summary: Inspired by Barney Bigard, then by Louis Armstrong at the Vendome and Keppard and Shoffner, he gave up saxophone for trumpet and recorded with Ma Rainey on soprano.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: At that time, cause I listened to quite a few saxophone players that I liked, like Barney Bigard, I thought he was the greatest saxophone player I ever heard in my life. At that time and so he inspired me to continue on the saxophone. At that time Louis Armstrong was with Fletcher Henderson, he was out of town, so he came back to Chicago, then I decided -- I said, well let me go to hear him so I went to hear him at the Vendome, I also heard him in Oliver's band, I think I -- quite sure I heard him in Oliver's band one year, I don't know what year that was, but that was before -- I used to go to Chicago in the summer sometimes, but I heard Louis Armstrong at the Vendome, then --

With Erskine Tate. Then that was my first time hearing of New Orleans musicians, I never heard of New Orleans musicians before. So then I went to hear Kneppard Freddie Kappel, and Bob Shoffner and then I got interested in that type of music and that's why I threw the saxophone away. I said the trumpet is more beautiful than saxophone and I just decided to ditch the saxophone altogether. During the time I was with Al, though, at the Dreamland I played saxophone

and then I started to play cornet, which he liked my cornet playing also, better. But he had a cornet player in the band recorded with at that time and we recall it was Ma Rainey there with Wynn Al Williams, I was playing soprano saxophone.
